In the 2026/27 tax year (6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027), adults aged 18 or over can pay up to £20,000 into ISAs. You can split that between cash ISAs, stocks and shares ISAs, innovative finance ISAs and a Lifetime ISA. The Lifetime ISA has its own limit of £4,000. Unused allowance does not carry forward.

From 6 April 2027, investors under 65 will be capped at £12,000 a year in cash ISAs. The overall £20,000 allowance stays the same.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The ISA allowance for 2026/27 is £20,000 for adults aged 18 or over. The tax year runs from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027. You can split the allowance between cash ISAs, stocks and shares ISAs, innovative finance ISAs and a Lifetime ISA. The Lifetime ISA has its own limit of £4,000. Unused allowance does not carry forward.

Changes from 6 April 2027 will cap cash ISA payments at £12,000 a year for investors under 65. The overall £20,000 allowance stays the same.

You can pay up to £4,000 a year into a Lifetime ISA. This counts towards the £20,000 overall ISA allowance. The government adds a 25% bonus of up to £1,000 a year.

A Lifetime ISA can be opened by anyone aged 18 to 39. Withdrawals for reasons other than those below incur a 25% government charge. The permitted reasons are:
- buying a first home costing £450,000 or less, once the account has been open for at least 12 months
- being aged 60 or over
- being terminally ill with less than 12 months to live

More detail is in the ISA guide on our website.

The documents describe these changes from 6 April 2027:

- Investors under 65 can pay at most £12,000 a tax year into cash ISAs. The overall £20,000 ISA allowance doesn't change, so the remainder can go into stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs. Investors aged 65 and over keep a £20,000 cash ISA limit.
- Transfers from stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs into cash ISAs will no longer be allowed.
- A charge will apply to interest paid on cash held inside a stocks and shares or innovative finance ISA.
- Money already in cash ISAs isn't affected by the cap.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

One related change: transfers from stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs into cash ISAs will no longer be permitted from that date.

The annual allowance is £60,000. If the total paid into your pensions in a tax year exceeds it, an annual allowance charge is normally due. That total includes employer contributions and the value of any defined benefit accrual.

- **Flexible withdrawals:** Once you have taken taxable income flexibly from a defined contribution pension, the money purchase annual allowance of £10,000 applies to further defined contribution contributions.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/
